name: POST /api/leadflow/failures/:id/retry - exactly one, then a human
description:
Claims the single retry a provider failure is allowed, then falls back to a HUMAN TASK (4cc3f597-f6c8-4dc5-8044-096ce144e676#AC3). MEASURED LIVE: the first call retried, the second returned human_task_required with the runbook fallback and its owner.

CLAIMED BY THE UPDATE, not decided by a read. Two concurrent handlers would both read retry_count = 0 and both retry - the customer gets two copies of the same message and the incident report says "we retried once".

NEVER A THIRD ATTEMPT. Retrying until it works is how a provider outage becomes a duplicate storm the moment it recovers: every queued attempt succeeds at once, into the same inboxes. Two automated attempts and then a person is the SOP, and the second refusal names the call-or-manual-email task rather than leaving the operator to infer it.
